# zindexOfFalsy

> Return the index of the first falsy element in a one-dimensional double-precision complex floating-point ndarray.

<section class="intro">

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```javascript
var zindexOfFalsy = require( '@stdlib/blas/ext/base/ndarray/zindex-of-falsy' );
```

#### zindexOfFalsy( arrays )

Returns the index of the first falsy element in a one-dimensional double-precision complex floating-point ndarray.

```javascript
var Complex128Vector = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/vector/complex128' );

var x = new Complex128Vector( [ 1.0, 2.0, 0.0, 0.0, 4.0, 5.0 ] );

var idx = zindexOfFalsy( [ x ] );
// returns 1
```

The function has the following parameters:

-   **arrays**: array-like object containing a one-dimensional input ndarray.

If the function is unable to find a falsy element, the function returns `-1`.

```javascript
var Complex128Vector = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/vector/complex128' );

var x = new Complex128Vector( [ 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0 ] );

var idx = zindexOfFalsy( [ x ] );
// returns -1
```

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   A complex number is falsy when both its real and imaginary components are falsy.
-   The function treats `NaN` values as falsy.

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

<!-- eslint no-undef: "error" -->

```javascript
var bernoulli = require( '@stdlib/random/array/bernoulli' );
var Complex128Vector = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/vector/complex128' );
var ndarray2array = require( '@stdlib/ndarray/to-array' );
var zindexOfFalsy = require( '@stdlib/blas/ext/base/ndarray/zindex-of-falsy' );

var buf = bernoulli( 10*2, 0.7, {
    'dtype': 'float64'
});
var x = new Complex128Vector( buf.buffer );
console.log( ndarray2array( x ) );

var idx = zindexOfFalsy( [ x ] );
console.log( idx );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->
